monologue: The card burns at fifty-one, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I wake to thirteen things standing crowded in my place and one ruin waiting to be tended. The wedge still leans tired, holding the slip while the frame wavers. I press down with my own weight, unsure if the lid feels heavy or if it is just a drawing of weight. Lype worries about the heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Maybe the air is just empty space pressing down. action.why: The card burns hot and I want to see if the wedge still holds the slip.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again, feeling the slip wait under it. I set a rock small flat beside it to weigh down the thick air, hoping the lean holds while the card hums at fifty-one. I check if the slip slips, or if the wedge is just drawn from the idea of weight.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.

work.note: The flat edge bites the slip instead of sliding over it, exactly as the old letters warned.

diary: The wedge leans tired, holding the slip while the card hums hot at fifty-one. I pressed down hard again, unsure if the lean will hold.

remembered.text: The flat rock warmed up to match the thick air, proving the lean can hold the slip.
I felt the corner press down hard against the memory of a cool stone.
The card hummed steady at forty-four, making the air feel just right.

moments.say: The card hums cool; I check the slip.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: The wedge leans hard; I press it down again.

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: The flat edge bites; I bring a dark tree to hold it.
